title.narrative: Helping Rohingya refugees pursue accountability and participate in international justice processes

description.narrative: Contract related to: Helping Rohingya refugees pursue accountability and participate in international justice processes - Rohingya refugees living in the camps in Cox¿s Bazar are experiencing an unprecedented rise in insecurity and inter and intra-communal tensions in their everyday lives. Food shortages, lack of livelihood opportunities, and the current intensification of fighting in Rakhine State in Myanmar have exacerbated the proliferation of criminal armed groups inside the camps. Insecurity and criminality are causing clashes, violence and serious protection incidents, including physical assaults, abductions and murders of Rohingya refugees. Restrictions to freedom of movement, desperation, hunger and hopelessness are also forcing an increasing number of Rohingya refugees to flee the camps and undertake perilous sea journeys across the Andaman Sea in search for protection and safety. Confusion, rumours as well as a distant and limited scope of the outcome of international judicial proceedings relating to the past crimes committed by the Myanmar military against the Rohingya are likely to create yet further risk of protest, unrest, and long-term loss of trust in an already strained environment.
